build/tools/docker_build.sh

Shell · Tier B

Build and validate Linux candidates before promoting compiled artifacts.

Usage

Use build/build on Linux x86_64; --help needs no Docker daemon. --validate-artifacts qualifies existing binaries.

Inputs

Local Unix-socket Docker, Git, flock, pinned linux-container.env and build options; release mode also requires the configured local GPG key.

Side effects

Locks output, snapshots source, builds containers, stages binaries and runs fresh-install validation. Successful candidates are finalized and promoted; signing uses the host keyring.

Cleanup

EXIT/INT/TERM cleanup stops the owned container/child and retains failure evidence. Verified download caches remain; successful disposable installation homes are removed.

@see build/README.md

build/tools/windows_acceptance.ps1

PowerShell · Tier B

Run Windows installation acceptance as a temporary standard user.

Usage

Elevated disposable CI runner only, with -Directory pointing at built artifacts.

Inputs

CI=true, RUNNER_TEMP, the current Python executable and an artifact directory writable by the temporary account.

Side effects

Creates a local user, grants read/execute and artifact-write ACLs, starts seclogon and runs setup/service/lifecycle acceptance with a separate credential.

Cleanup

finally removes the temporary account and child/config scripts. ACL changes, profile files and service state are left to runner disposal.

@see build/tools/acceptance.py
